title: The Wobbly Seesaw Surprise
markdown:
The sun shone like a giant happy button, and Iris and Momo were at the park. Iris saw patterns in everything: clouds, leaves, the way the path stones repeated. Momo the monkey loved to leap and bound and make funny faces. He had just finished a banana, which made him extra bouncy, ready for playtime.

They ran to the seesaw, feet thudding on soft grass. It looked fine — smooth, red, ready. Momo, a rather big strong monkey, sat on one end. Down, down, down. The plank practically kissed the grass. Iris, a bit lighter, sat on the other. Her end barely moved. It wiggled in the air like a little wave goodbye.

“It’s all wobbly!” giggled Momo, jumping on his end, making it worse. The whole park seemed to wobble with him. They wanted to play. It was not working.

“Hmm.” Iris tapped her chin, eyes narrowed at the tricky tilt. “It’s not finding its pattern. A puzzle with missing pieces.” She looked at Momo’s curious furry face, then at the plank that seemed to have a mind of its own. “When you sit, ker-PLUNK. A big rock landing. When I sit, tip-tap. A little butterfly.”

They tried switching sides, thinking the seesaw was playing a trick. Momo sat on Iris’s side. Ker-PLUNK. Down he went. Iris sat on Momo’s side. Tip-tap-wobble. One side got all the down-time; the other got all the up-time. Not fair at all.

Teacher June walked by, humming a tune like sunshine. Smile warm as a blanket. “What’s all the seesaw silliness?”

Iris explained. “It only goes down when Momo sits, and barely moves when I do. As if it only likes one of us.”

June sat on the grass. “Seesaws like to be balanced. A team effort.” She left the best-friends-and-fairness speech for later, if ever. “Iris, you see patterns. What do you notice about how it moves when you both sit?”

Iris squinted. Momo was way down, monkey toes almost in the dandelions. She was way up, high enough to tickle the lowest oak leaves. “Momo is heavier. I am lighter. The seesaw feels that difference. A BIG difference.”

“Exactly. And when Momo sits near the very, very end?”

Iris watched his toes. At the far end, her side shot way up. When he wiggled a little closer to the middle, her end did not fly so high — just a bit. “When he’s far away, my side goes UP really high! When he moves closer to the middle, mine comes down a bit!”

“That’s what I see!” Momo’s tail flicked. “When I move, your side moves!”

June beamed. “You’ve found the pattern. How can you use that dance so it goes up and down together, smooth?”

Iris looked at Momo. Momo looked at Iris. She looked at his gripping feet, then at the painted middle of the plank. “What if you don’t sit right on the very end? What if you scoot a little closer to the middle, where it looks strongest?”

Momo, always ready if giggles were promised, scooted in. Iris sat. Her end went up, his went down — but not as far. The seesaw took a deep breath instead of a gasp.

“Ooh! Closer. More friendly now!”

Iris grinned. “What if I come closer too? Maybe we meet in the middle?” She scooted in. Momo, feeling brave, edged out a tiny bit from where he was.

Then their ends went down and up, down and up, a smooth gentle rhythm. A perfect song. Giggle. Giggle. Balancing. His side down, hers up; hers down, his up. The plank sang as they moved together.

“We did it!” Momo bounced, and this time the bounce only made the rhythm smoother.

Iris clapped, a happy beat against the hum. “Balance. When one side goes down, the other comes up — but not quite so far. A seesaw team.”

June nodded and named it once: balance. Right spots. Up and down nicely. She did not compare toys or turns.

Iris looked at the plank, then at Momo. “Balance.” Her pattern brain whirred, but she did not list bananas on heads or juggling with feet. She kept the next scoot ready. They saw-sawed, up and down, the delightful rhythm of having found the missing pieces, and left the oak leaves untickled for now.
